name: Escape Dead Orchard Control
summary: Exiting Dead Orchard requires opening the high leg triangle safely; the bottom player releases the control while the top player protects the captured arms.
description: Exiting Dead Orchard requires opening the high leg triangle safely; the bottom player releases the control while the top player protects the captured arms.
overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Dead Orchard Control, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. The listed bottom seat is the holder of the real guard. Headlock arm extraction is not a direct defense against the both-arm leg triangle.

The bottom player faces the opponent and keeps the hips close beneath the shoulders. The legs form a high figure-four around the shoulder line, with both opposing arms inside. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Nathan Orchard — Dead Orchard, part 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XoiB1D2WJwE); [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo).

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (bottom): What are you releasing at the start?
flashcards.answer: The bottom performer holds Dead Orchard and is resetting the both-arm leg triangle.
flashcards.answer_line: A high leg triangle around both arms

plausible: High triangle with one arm outside
Low ankles crossed around the waist
trap: Two high shins with no figure-four

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (bottom): What should end before opening the legs?
flashcards.answer: Remove wrist and elbow loading before opening the high enclosure and allowing the arms to move.
flashcards.answer_line: Wrist leverage on a captured elbow

plausible: Only the hand supporting the shin
Only the squeeze from the high legs
trap: Only head pull; keep wrist leverage

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (bottom): How should the high leg return lower?
flashcards.answer: Open the figure-four and lower the leg through the hip instead of wrenching the foot.

plausible: Pull foot while the knee stays fixed
Turn ankle with the thigh still
trap: Turn torso before opening the legs

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (bottom): What replaces the high leg barrier as space opens?
flashcards.answer: Restore inside forearms and knees during the released guard-recovery phase.

plausible: Forearms in with both knees outside
Knees in with elbows reaching away
trap: Chase wrists while knees drop wide

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (bottom): Where should your shoulders and hips remain directed?
flashcards.answer: Keep facing the opponent while rebuilding guard; turning away is not the stated reset.

plausible: Shoulders away; hips face opponent
Hips face away; chest toward them
trap: Both away before the knee returns

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (bottom): What permits a new attack after the reset?
flashcards.answer: Re-establish usable inside knee space and comfortable posture before starting another attack.

plausible: Loose wrist grip with knees bypassed
Shoulder frame with both knees out
trap: Feet raised with hips still awkward

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard: which parts of the top opponent are inside your high triangle?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player owns the leg trap, and the top player's arms are the captured limbs.

plausible: Only their near arm
Only their forearms

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (bottom): Which restraint must open for this reset?
flashcards.answer: This reset opens a high leg triangle; a front-headlock hand-grip escape addresses a different structure.
flashcards.answer_line: Legs around both arms and shoulders

plausible: One high shin with both elbows free
Ankles crossed low at the waist

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (bottom): With both hands trapped, how can your partner tap?
flashcards.answer: Both-arm capture can remove hand-tap access; agree on verbal and foot signals and release promptly.
flashcards.answer_line: A verbal stop or a foot tap

plausible: Withdraw trapped hand before signal
Wait for legs to open to hand-tap
trap: Use only a hand signal from the trap

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (bottom): What keeps a crossface from filling the recovery space?
flashcards.answer: After full arm release, use a forearm barrier and a small hip escape to recover inside knee space.
flashcards.answer_line: An inside forearm on their shoulder

plausible: Hand on wrist with elbow outside
Forearm outside the approaching arm
trap: Hands at hip without an upper frame

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (top): What threat persists even without neck pressure?
flashcards.answer: A comfortable neck does not make the captured elbows safe in Dead Orchard.
flashcards.answer_line: Short arm lock from both-arm capture

plausible: Only a neck attack with one arm out
Only wrist bending; elbow unloaded
trap: No arm lock until shoulders are free

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (top): Which action offers the attacker an elbow lever?
flashcards.answer: Orchard's demonstration exploits a straightened arm; do not offer that lever while forcing posture.
flashcards.answer_line: Straight arm between the high legs

plausible: Elbow bent and close to the torso
Wait for the shoulder trap to open
trap: Move shoulder and elbow once free

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (top): What is an early hip frame meant to interrupt?
flashcards.answer: Before the high figure-four closes, a hip or thigh frame can preserve space against the shoulder-level climb. It is not a late escape guarantee after both arms are trapped.
flashcards.answer_line: High legs closing over the shoulders

plausible: Elbow extending after leg closure
Wrist grip added to fixed shoulders
trap: Head rising after both arms are free

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (top): What lets the shoulder and elbow withdraw together?
flashcards.answer: Use actual shoulder clearance through the opened legs, stopping if the arm is already loaded.

plausible: Wrist pulled with shoulder fixed
Chin lifted above their shin
trap: One foot down; other pins the arm

flashcards.question: Escape Dead Orchard Control (top): What is the checkpoint before lifting your chest?
flashcards.answer: Recover upright posture after the shoulder line clears, not by dragging the trapped elbows upward.

plausible: One fingertip outside the legs
Only their wrist grip releases
trap: Feet step back with arms still fixed
